text:
alex: Noticed a weird spike — ~2.7% of prod traffic is landing on v1 even when clients send X-API-Version: v2. Dashboard cohort name is 'legacy-header-multi' :eyes:

maya: huh. is that traffic actually getting rewritten or is the routing decision missing the header?

alex: From traces it looks like the header parser is treating comma-separated version values as unknown. Example header: `X-API-Version: v2,v1` -> our header normalizer currently picks first token naively.

jon: That header shape comes from some SDK proxies that append the version instead of replacing. We saw this in staging but rate was tiny.

sam: can we make the routing more defensive rather than silently falling back to v1? Bad failure mode is silent downgrade under quota logic. :grimacing:

alex: Agreed. Proposal: create a 'handshake-quarantine' shadow cohort for requests where header parsing yields >1 token or unexpected tokens. Route them to v2 by default (to avoid silent downgrades) but mark telemetry and stop counting against v2 quota for 72h while we investigate.

maya: +1 for quarantine cohort. We should also tag those requests with `version_mismatch=true` and `legacy_header=true` so console filters can find them.

jon: Operationally: two parts — (1) change routing priority so explicit header tokens prefer the highest-compatible version (v2 over v1) instead of fallback, (2) mark them as shadow/quarantine so quota/billing unaffected until we clear.

sheila: For Console UX: add a dashboard widget 'Quarantine cohort: header anomalies' with top client ids, rate, and last 7d trend. Also a notice in rollout page if cohort >1% so PMs get pinged.

sam: Quick code sketch for the parse change:
```python
vals = [v.strip() for v in req.headers.get('x-api-version','').split(',') if v.strip()]
if not vals:
    route = default_route(req)
else:
    # prefer newest stabler version available
    route = choose_preferred_version(vals, prefer=['v2','v1'])
```
This prevents taking the trailing v1 token by accident.

alex: Nice. For telemetry, propose we emit `routing_decision_reason` with values: `explicit_preferred`, `legacy_quarantine`, `missing_header` to avoid ambiguous signals.

maya: We also need a sampling policy — don't want to create noise. Start with 100% capture for quarantine cohort (they're small) and 1% shadow for other header anomalies.

jon: Rollout plan: feature-flag the parsing change behind `quarantine-v1-legacy` flag, enable in prod to 5% of traffic first, monitor error and latency dashboards for 2 hours, then bump to 100% if green. If we see more than 0.5% increase in token cost per request we roll back.

ops-bot: FYI: created ticket INF-2458 to track quarantine cohort + telemetry.

alex: I'll add a short runbook for oncall:
- If quarantine rate >1% and rising: check top client ids in Console -> quarantine widget
- If top clients are internal proxies -> contact infra slack channel and ask for header normalization fix
- If error rate or latency increases -> rollback flag `quarantine-v1-legacy`

jon: Can eng-platform add a lightweight console badge that surfaces at-route-level: "header anomalies detected (quarantine)" with quick link to runbook?

sheila: Yep — I'll queue a small UI card. Should be non-blocking; 1 day touch.

maya: One more ask: ensure we don't count quarantine traffic towards per-route quota throttles. We can mark requests with `quarantine=true` and the quota service should ignore them. Otherwise customers may get unexpected 429s.

alex: Good call. I'll update the PR to set a `quota_ignore` flag for quarantine paths.

sre-bot: Alert subscription: added monitoring for metric `quarantine_cohort_rate` and will page if >3% sustained for 5m.

sam: ok sounds actionable. I'll own the flag rollout and the parsing change, pinging infra teams for SDK proxies list.

alex: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the canonical discussion. Will post PR and link ticket once ready. :thumbsup:
